chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Salimah, the freedwoman of the son of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when death approached him, and he fainted; when he regained consciousness, he said, 'Give al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali (who is al-Aftas) seventy dinars.'
I said to him, 'Do you give a man who struck you with the blade?' He said, 'Woe to you, do you not read the Quran?'
'Did you not hear the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And those who connect what Allah has ordered to be connected, and fear their Lord and fear the evil reckoning'.'

key_terms.الْأَفْطَسُ: al-Aftas (a title meaning 'the one with the broad forehead', referring to al-Hasan ibn Ali)
key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: the evil reckoning / bad accounting on Judgment Day
key_terms.يَصِلُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ ي: connecting what Allah has ordered to be connected (referring to kinship)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq give money to the man who injured him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs the giving of seventy dinars to al-Aftas, a man who had struck him with a blade, to illustrate the principle of *sila al-rahim* (maintaining kinship ties) even amidst personal injury. By citing Surah Ar-Ra'd, the Imam emphasizes that fulfilling divine commands regarding family bonds supersedes individual grievances, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence for resolving familial disputes. This incident highlights the spiritual merit of forgiving relatives and maintaining social cohesion within the extended family structure.
